overall: A neighbour who has stood at that creek telling you how a Gulf coast town keeps watch, warm and dry, with no hush and no sales lilt. The read starts easy and observational, dips to its quietest at the fact that there were no sensors, lifts gently through the how, and settles lower and more certain at the close.

lines.text: In Friendswood, people come outside and look at the creek every day.
lines.intent: Set the scene as an ordinary habit, not an alarm
lines.note: Conversational, a little smile in it. Weight on creek. Friendswood said plainly, FRENDZ-wood, no stress on the place name.

lines.text: Jason Jones, who sits on the local drainage board, says it is almost like PTSD from Harvey and other rain events.
lines.intent: Quote the feeling gently and let the speaker own it
lines.note: Handle Harvey flat and kind, no drop in the voice and no dramatic weight. Say PTSD as a plain fact, lightly attributed. Weight on Harvey, then let the line end level.

lines.text: That fear has a ranking. The board's president, Rusty Burkett, calls flooding and drainage the number one threat to lives and property in Galveston County.
lines.intent: Turn from feeling to official stakes
lines.note: First sentence short and dry. Second reads like reporting a quote, even and unhurried. Weight on number one. Galveston is GAL-vez-tun.

lines.text: Yet until this spring, Jones says, the county had no flood sensors at all.
lines.note: Quietest line of the piece. Deliver it flat with no lift, understated and a touch wry. Weight on none, last words fall away.

lines.text: So in April, the Galveston County Consolidated Drainage District switched on seven radar sensors, six in the Clear Creek watershed and one in the Dickinson Bayou watershed. Each cost less than ten thousand dollars.
lines.intent: Deliver the concrete fix and its modest price
lines.note: First lift of the read, brisk and matter of fact. Keep the six and one split clean. Weight on seven. The price sentence is dry, almost an aside, weight on less than ten thousand.

lines.text: One reading is one spot on one creek. So the system adds rainfall totals, stream gauges, weather stations and how soaked the soil already is.
lines.intent: Explain how one sensor becomes a picture
lines.note: Names read plainly as a list of facts. The one spot on one creek sentence is the thinking beat, slower and slightly lower. Then the list moves at an easy walking pace. Axonis is ax-OH-nis.

lines.text: Then AI tools help predict how a flood could develop, even how conditions upstream could affect neighborhoods downstream.
lines.intent: Name the AI role without hype
lines.note: Keep it modest, the AI mention gets no extra shine. Gentle contrast of upstream and downstream, weight on downstream.

lines.text: Residents see it as a map. Green means safe. Yellow, flooding possible. Red, flooding likely.
lines.intent: Make the output tangible and simple
lines.note: Light and clear, the three colours as a small pattern with an even rhythm. Red is the same level as green, no menace, no rise at the end.

lines.text: They can sign up for alerts on one creek, and the platform is set to text them when the water rises to a level officials set.
lines.intent: Show the practical reach, a text on a phone
lines.note: Plain and helpful, like explaining it across a fence. Weight on text.

lines.text: The map does not decide anything. Jones says it helps people choose whether a road is still passable, or whether it is time to leave.
lines.intent: State the human limit of the tool
lines.note: The first sentence is firm and flat, a quiet correction. Second is warm and unforced, no worry in the voice. Weight on choose. Time to leave said as an everyday decision.

lines.text: Seven sensors are a start. The district maintains more than 80 miles of creeks, ditches and bayous, and executive director Paige Bailey says the system has already mapped where it needs more gauges.
lines.intent: Give honest scale and the next step
lines.note: Seven sensors are a start is dry and a little rueful. Then read the 80 miles as eighty miles, even and factual. Weight on more gauges. Bayous is BYE-yoos.

lines.text: For now, it covers only Friendswood and League City. People still walk out to look at the creek. Now the creek can answer back.
lines.intent: Close on the human habit, with a small wry turn
lines.note: Settle lower and more certain than the middle. Walk out to look at the creek is simple and affectionate. The last line is the driest of the piece, said quietly with a half smile and no lift at the end.
